pr.title: docs: add custom Blacksmith's Forge theme for DocFX site

report.summary: This PR replaces the DocFX site stylesheet (docfx/templates/forgemap/public/main.css) with a full custom "Blacksmith's Forge" theme — new color variables, typography, navbar/footer/search styling, code/table/TOC styling, transitions and reduced-motion handling — and changes the docs deployment concurrency settings in .github/workflows/docs.yml. The CSS is documentation-only, but two changes have real behavior impact: the Pages concurrency key/cancel semantics, and a few global rules (transparent gradient heading text, table overflow clipping, dark-mode search field variable inversion). Reviewers should focus on deployment serialization and on whether the global `!important` overrides break readability in dark/high-contrast modes.

suggestions.title: Pages concurrency key split by ref allows overlapping deployments
suggestions.reason: The diff replaces the shared Pages lock with a per-ref key and flips cancellation on: `group: "pages-${{ github.ref }}"` (docs.yml:26) and `cancel-in-progress: true` (docs.yml:27). Previously every docs run shared the single `pages` group, which serialized deploys to the GitHub Pages environment; including `github.ref` in the key means runs triggered from different refs (e.g. main plus a release/docs branch that also runs this workflow on push) fall into different concurrency groups and are no longer mutually exclusive, so two `deploy` jobs can target the same Pages environment at the same time. `cancel-in-progress: true` additionally allows an in-flight deploy job to be killed mid-publish, which the official Pages starter workflow explicitly avoids (`cancel-in-progress: false`).
suggestions.recommendation: Keep a single lock for the deployment target and let production deploys finish, e.g. restore `group: "pages"` with `cancel-in-progress: false`; if you only want to cancel *build* runs, put the cancellation on the build job and leave the deploy job in the shared `pages` group (job-level `concurrency` on the deploy job).
suggestions.failure_scenario: A push to main starts a Pages deploy; before its `deploy` job finishes, a push to a second ref that triggers the same workflow starts another run. Because the groups now differ, GitHub does not queue or cancel it, and both runs call actions/deploy-pages against the same Pages environment: the newer main content can be replaced by the older ref's artifact, and a run cancelled mid-deploy leaves the docs site stale with a failed deploy job.
